[887](https://docs.rs#887)
[888](https://docs.rs#888)/// De/Serialize Durations as number of seconds.
[889](https://docs.rs#889)///
[890](https://docs.rs#890)/// De/serialize durations as number of seconds with sub-second precision.
[891](https://docs.rs#891)/// Sub-second precision is *only* supported for [`DurationSecondsWithFrac`], but not for [`DurationSeconds`].
[892](https://docs.rs#892)/// You can configure the serialization format between integers, floats, and stringified numbers with the `FORMAT` specifier and configure the deserialization with the `STRICTNESS` specifier.
[893](https://docs.rs#893)///
[894](https://docs.rs#894)/// The `STRICTNESS` specifier can either be [`formats::Strict`] or [`formats::Flexible`] and defaults to [`formats::Strict`].
[895](https://docs.rs#895)/// [`formats::Strict`] means that deserialization only supports the type given in `FORMAT`, e.g., if `FORMAT` is `u64` deserialization from a `f64` will error.
[896](https://docs.rs#896)/// [`formats::Flexible`] means that deserialization will perform a best effort to extract the correct duration and allows deserialization from any type.
[897](https://docs.rs#897)/// For example, deserializing `DurationSeconds<f64, Flexible>` will discard any subsecond precision during deserialization from `f64` and will parse a `String` as an integer number.
[898](https://docs.rs#898)/// Serialization of integers will round the duration to the nearest value.
[899](https://docs.rs#899)///
[900](https://docs.rs#900)/// This type also supports [`chrono::Duration`] with the `chrono_0_4`-[feature flag].
[901](https://docs.rs#901)/// This type also supports [`time::Duration`][::time_0_3::Duration] with the `time_0_3`-[feature flag].
[902](https://docs.rs#902)///
[903](https://docs.rs#903)/// This table lists the available `FORMAT`s for the different duration types.
[904](https://docs.rs#904)/// The `FORMAT` specifier defaults to `u64`/`f64`.
[905](https://docs.rs#905)///
[906](https://docs.rs#906)/// | Duration Type         | Converter                 | Available `FORMAT`s      |
[907](https://docs.rs#907)/// | --------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------ |
[908](https://docs.rs#908)/// | `std::time::Duration` | `DurationSeconds`         | *`u64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[909](https://docs.rs#909)/// | `std::time::Duration` | `DurationSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[910](https://docs.rs#910)/// | `chrono::Duration`    | `DurationSeconds`         | `i64`, `f64`, `String`   |
[911](https://docs.rs#911)/// | `chrono::Duration`    | `DurationSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[912](https://docs.rs#912)/// | `time::Duration`      | `DurationSeconds`         | `i64`, `f64`, `String`   |
[913](https://docs.rs#913)/// | `time::Duration`      | `DurationSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[914](https://docs.rs#914)///
[915](https://docs.rs#915)/// # Examples
[916](https://docs.rs#916)///
[917](https://docs.rs#917)/// ```rust
[918](https://docs.rs#918)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[919](https://docs.rs#919)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[920](https://docs.rs#920)/// # use serde_json::json;
[921](https://docs.rs#921)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, DurationSeconds};
[922](https://docs.rs#922)/// use std::time::Duration;
[923](https://docs.rs#923)///
[924](https://docs.rs#924)/// #[serde_as]
[925](https://docs.rs#925)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[926](https://docs.rs#926)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[927](https://docs.rs#927)/// struct Durations {
[928](https://docs.rs#928)///     #[serde_as(as = "DurationSeconds<u64>")]
[929](https://docs.rs#929)///     d_u64: Duration,
[930](https://docs.rs#930)///     #[serde_as(as = "DurationSeconds<f64>")]
[931](https://docs.rs#931)///     d_f64: Duration,
[932](https://docs.rs#932)///     #[serde_as(as = "DurationSeconds<String>")]
[933](https://docs.rs#933)///     d_string: Duration,
[934](https://docs.rs#934)/// }
[935](https://docs.rs#935)///
[936](https://docs.rs#936)/// // Serialization
[937](https://docs.rs#937)/// // See how the values get rounded, since subsecond precision is not allowed.
[938](https://docs.rs#938)///
[939](https://docs.rs#939)/// let d = Durations {
[940](https://docs.rs#940)///     d_u64: Duration::new(12345, 0), // Create from seconds and nanoseconds
[941](https://docs.rs#941)///     d_f64: Duration::new(12345, 500_000_000),
[942](https://docs.rs#942)///     d_string: Duration::new(12345, 999_999_999),
[943](https://docs.rs#943)/// };
[944](https://docs.rs#944)/// // Observe the different data types
[945](https://docs.rs#945)/// let expected = json!({
[946](https://docs.rs#946)///     "d_u64": 12345,
[947](https://docs.rs#947)///     "d_f64": 12346.0,
[948](https://docs.rs#948)///     "d_string": "12346",
[949](https://docs.rs#949)/// });
[950](https://docs.rs#950)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(d).unwrap());
[951](https://docs.rs#951)///
[952](https://docs.rs#952)/// // Deserialization works too
[953](https://docs.rs#953)/// // Subsecond precision in numbers will be rounded away
[954](https://docs.rs#954)///
[955](https://docs.rs#955)/// let json = json!({
[956](https://docs.rs#956)///     "d_u64": 12345,
[957](https://docs.rs#957)///     "d_f64": 12345.5,
[958](https://docs.rs#958)///     "d_string": "12346",
[959](https://docs.rs#959)/// });
[960](https://docs.rs#960)/// let expected = Durations {
[961](https://docs.rs#961)///     d_u64: Duration::new(12345, 0), // Create from seconds and nanoseconds
[962](https://docs.rs#962)///     d_f64: Duration::new(12346, 0),
[963](https://docs.rs#963)///     d_string: Duration::new(12346, 0),
[964](https://docs.rs#964)/// };
[965](https://docs.rs#965)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap());
[966](https://docs.rs#966)/// # }
[967](https://docs.rs#967)/// ```

[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)/// De/Serialize timestamps as seconds since the UNIX epoch
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)///
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)/// De/serialize timestamps as seconds since the UNIX epoch.
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)/// Subsecond precision is *only* supported for [`TimestampSecondsWithFrac`], but not for [`TimestampSeconds`].
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)/// You can configure the serialization format between integers, floats, and stringified numbers with the `FORMAT` specifier and configure the deserialization with the `STRICTNESS` specifier.
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)/// Serialization of integers will round the timestamp to the nearest value.
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)///
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)/// The `STRICTNESS` specifier can either be [`formats::Strict`] or [`formats::Flexible`] and defaults to [`formats::Strict`].
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)/// [`formats::Strict`] means that deserialization only supports the type given in `FORMAT`, e.g., if `FORMAT` is `i64` deserialization from a `f64` will error.
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)/// [`formats::Flexible`] means that deserialization will perform a best effort to extract the correct timestamp and allows deserialization from any type.
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)/// For example, deserializing `TimestampSeconds<f64, Flexible>` will discard any subsecond precision during deserialization from `f64` and will parse a `String` as an integer number.
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)///
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)/// This type also supports [`chrono::DateTime`] with the `chrono_0_4`-[feature flag].
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)/// This type also supports [`time::OffsetDateTime`][::time_0_3::OffsetDateTime] and [`time::PrimitiveDateTime`][::time_0_3::PrimitiveDateTime] with the `time_0_3`-[feature flag].
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)///
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)/// This table lists the available `FORMAT`s for the different timestamp types.
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)/// The `FORMAT` specifier defaults to `i64` or `f64`.
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)///
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)/// | Timestamp Type            | Converter                  | Available `FORMAT`s      |
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)/// | ------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------ |
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)/// | `std::time::SystemTime`   | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)/// | `std::time::SystemTime`   | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)/// | `chrono::DateTime<Utc>`   | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)/// | `chrono::DateTime<Utc>`   | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)/// | `chrono::DateTime<Local>` | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)/// | `chrono::DateTime<Local>` | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)/// | `chrono::NaiveDateTime`   | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)/// | `chrono::NaiveDateTime`   | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)/// | `time::OffsetDateTime`    | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)/// | `time::OffsetDateTime`    | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)/// | `time::PrimitiveDateTime` | `TimestampSeconds`         | *`i64`*, `f64`, `String` |
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)/// | `time::PrimitiveDateTime` | `TimestampSecondsWithFrac` | *`f64`*, `String`        |
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)///
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)/// # Examples
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)///
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)/// ```rust
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, TimestampSeconds};
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)/// use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)///
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)/// #[serde_as]
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)/// struct Timestamps {
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<i64>")]
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)///     st_i64: SystemTime,
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<f64>")]
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)///     st_f64: SystemTime,
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<String>")]
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)///     st_string: SystemTime,
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)/// }
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)///
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)/// // Serialization
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)/// // See how the values get rounded, since subsecond precision is not allowed.
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)///
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)/// let ts = Timestamps {
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)///     st_i64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 0)).unwrap(),
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)///     st_f64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 500_000_000)).unwrap(),
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)///     st_string: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 999_999_999)).unwrap(),
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)/// };
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)/// // Observe the different data types
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)/// let expected = json!({
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)///     "st_i64": 12345,
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)///     "st_f64": 12346.0,
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)///     "st_string": "12346",
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)/// });
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(ts).unwrap());
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)///
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)/// // Deserialization works too
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)/// // Subsecond precision in numbers will be rounded away
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)///
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)/// let json = json!({
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)///     "st_i64": 12345,
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)///     "st_f64": 12345.5,
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)///     "st_string": "12346",
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)/// });
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)/// let expected  = Timestamps {
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)///     st_i64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 0)).unwrap(),
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)///     st_f64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12346, 0)).unwrap(),
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)///     st_string: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12346, 0)).unwrap(),
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)/// };
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap());
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)/// # }
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)/// ```
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)///
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)/// [`chrono::DateTime<Utc>`] and [`chrono::DateTime<Local>`] are also supported when using the `chrono` feature.
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)/// Like [`SystemTime`], it is a signed timestamp, thus can be de/serialized as an `i64`.
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)///
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)/// ```rust

[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)/// # /* Ugliness to make the docs look nicer since I want to hide the rename of the chrono crate
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)/// use chrono::{DateTime, Local, TimeZone, Utc};
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)/// # */

[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)/// #[serde_as]

[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)/// struct Timestamps {
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<i64>")]
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)///     dt_i64: DateTime<Utc>,
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<f64>")]
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)///     dt_f64: DateTime<Local>,
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSeconds<String>")]
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)///     dt_string: DateTime<Utc>,
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)/// }
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)///
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)/// // Serialization
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)/// // See how the values get rounded, since subsecond precision is not allowed.
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)///
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)/// let ts = Timestamps {
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)///     dt_i64: Utc.timestamp_opt(-12345, 0).unwrap(),
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)///     dt_f64: Local.timestamp_opt(-12345, 500_000_000).unwrap(),
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)///     dt_string: Utc.timestamp_opt(12345, 999_999_999).unwrap(),
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)/// };
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)/// // Observe the different data types
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)/// let expected = json!({
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)///     "dt_i64": -12345,
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)///     "dt_f64": -12345.0,
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)///     "dt_string": "12346",
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)/// });
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(ts).unwrap());
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)///
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)/// // Deserialization works too
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)/// // Subsecond precision in numbers will be rounded away
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)///
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)/// let json = json!({
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)///     "dt_i64": -12345,
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)///     "dt_f64": -12345.5,
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)///     "dt_string": "12346",
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)/// });
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)/// let expected = Timestamps {

[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)///     dt_f64: Local.timestamp_opt(-12346, 0).unwrap(),
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)///     dt_string: Utc.timestamp_opt(12346, 0).unwrap(),
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)/// };

[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSecondsWithFrac<f64>")]
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)///     st_f64: SystemTime,
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSecondsWithFrac<String>")]
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)///     st_string: SystemTime,
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)/// }
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)///
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)/// // Serialization
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)/// // See how the values get rounded, since subsecond precision is not allowed.
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)///
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)/// let ts = Timestamps {
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)///     st_f64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 500_000_000)).unwrap(),
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)///     st_string: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 999_999_000)).unwrap(),
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)/// };
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)/// // Observe the different data types
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)/// let expected = json!({
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)///     "st_f64": 12345.5,
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)///     "st_string": "12345.999999",
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)/// });
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(ts).unwrap());
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)///
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)/// // Deserialization works too
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)/// // Subsecond precision in numbers will be rounded away
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)///
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)/// let json = json!({
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)///     "st_f64": 12345.5,
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)///     "st_string": "12345.987654",
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)/// });
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)/// let expected = Timestamps {
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)///     st_f64: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 500_000_000)).unwrap(),
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)///     st_string: SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH.checked_add(Duration::new(12345, 987_654_000)).unwrap(),
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)/// };
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap());
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)/// # }
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)/// ```
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)///
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)/// [`chrono::DateTime<Utc>`] and [`chrono::DateTime<Local>`] are also supported when using the `chrono_0_4` feature.
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)/// Like [`SystemTime`], it is a signed timestamp, thus can be de/serialized as an `i64`.
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)///
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)/// ```rust
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)/// # #[cfg(all(feature = "macros", feature = "chrono_0_4"))] {
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, TimestampSecondsWithFrac};
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)/// # use chrono_0_4::{DateTime, Local, TimeZone, Utc};
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)/// # /* Ugliness to make the docs look nicer since I want to hide the rename of the chrono crate
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)/// use chrono::{DateTime, Local, TimeZone, Utc};
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)/// # */
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)///
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)/// #[serde_as]
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)/// struct Timestamps {
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSecondsWithFrac<f64>")]
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)///     dt_f64: DateTime<Utc>,
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)///     #[serde_as(as = "TimestampSecondsWithFrac<String>")]
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)///     dt_string: DateTime<Local>,
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)/// }
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)///
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)/// // Serialization
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)///
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)/// let ts = Timestamps {
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)///     dt_f64: Utc.timestamp_opt(-12345, 500_000_000).unwrap(),
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)///     dt_string: Local.timestamp_opt(12345, 999_999_000).unwrap(),
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)/// };
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)/// // Observe the different data types
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)/// let expected = json!({
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)///     "dt_f64": -12344.5,
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)///     "dt_string": "12345.999999",
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)/// });
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(ts).unwrap());
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)///
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)/// // Deserialization works too
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)///
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)/// let json = json!({
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)///     "dt_f64": -12344.5,
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)///     "dt_string": "12345.987",
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)/// });
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)/// let expected = Timestamps {
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)///     dt_f64: Utc.timestamp_opt(-12345, 500_000_000).unwrap(),
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)///     dt_string: Local.timestamp_opt(12345, 987_000_000).unwrap(),
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)/// };
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::from_value(json).unwrap());
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)/// # }
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)/// ```
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)///
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)/// [`SystemTime`]: std::time::SystemTime
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)/// [`chrono::DateTime`]: ::chrono_0_4::DateTime

[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)/// Optimized handling of owned and borrowed byte representations.
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)///
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)/// Serialization of byte sequences like `&[u8]` or `Vec<u8>` is quite inefficient since each value will be serialized individually.
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)/// This converter type optimizes the serialization and deserialization.
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)///
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)/// This is a port of the [`serde_bytes`] crate making it compatible with the `serde_as` annotation, which allows it to be used in more cases than provided by [`serde_bytes`].
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)///
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)/// The type provides de/serialization for these types:
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)///
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)/// * `[u8; N]`, not possible using `serde_bytes`
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)/// * `&[u8; N]`, not possible using `serde_bytes`
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)/// * `&[u8]`
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)/// * `Box<[u8; N]>`, not possible using `serde_bytes`
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)/// * `Box<[u8]>`
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)/// * `Vec<u8>`
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)/// * `Cow<'_, [u8]>`
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)/// * `Cow<'_, [u8; N]>`, not possible using `serde_bytes`
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)///
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)/// [`serde_bytes`]: https://crates.io/crates/serde_bytes
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)///
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)/// # Examples
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)///
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)/// ```
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, Bytes};
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)/// # use std::borrow::Cow;
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)/// #
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)/// #[serde_as]
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)/// struct Test<'a> {
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)///     array: [u8; 15],
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)///     boxed: Box<[u8]>,
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)///     #[serde(borrow)]
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)///     cow: Cow<'a, [u8]>,
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)///     #[serde(borrow)]
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)///     cow_array: Cow<'a, [u8; 15]>,
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)///     vec: Vec<u8>,
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)/// }
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)///
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)/// let value = Test {
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)///     array: *b"0123456789ABCDE",
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)///     boxed: b"...".to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)///     cow: Cow::Borrowed(b"FooBar"),
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)///     cow_array: Cow::Borrowed(&[42u8; 15]),
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)///     vec: vec![0x41, 0x61, 0x21],
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)/// };
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)/// let expected = r#"(
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)///     array: b"0123456789ABCDE",
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)///     boxed: b"...",
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)///     cow: b"FooBar",
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)///     cow_array: b"***************",
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)///     vec: b"Aa!",
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)/// )"#;
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)///
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)/// # let pretty_config = ron::ser::PrettyConfig::new().new_line("\n");
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)/// assert_eq!(expected, ron::ser::to_string_pretty(&value, pretty_config).unwrap());
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)/// assert_eq!(value, ron::from_str(expected).unwrap());
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)/// # }
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)/// ```
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)///
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)/// Fully borrowed types can also be used but you'll need a Deserializer that
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)/// supports Serde's 0-copy deserialization:
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)///
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)/// ```
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, Bytes};
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)/// #
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)/// #[serde_as]
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)/// struct TestBorrows<'a> {
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)///     #[serde(borrow)]
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)///     array_buf: &'a [u8; 15],
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)///     #[serde_as(as = "Bytes")]
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)///     #[serde(borrow)]
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)///     buf: &'a [u8],
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)/// }
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)///
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)/// let value = TestBorrows {
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)///     array_buf: &[10u8; 15],
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)///     buf: &[20u8, 21u8, 22u8],
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)/// };
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)/// let expected = r#"(
[1650](https://docs.rs#1650)///     array_buf: b"\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n\n",
[1651](https://docs.rs#1651)///     buf: b"\x14\x15\x16",
[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)/// )"#;
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)///
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)/// # let pretty_config = ron::ser::PrettyConfig::new().new_line("\n");
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)/// assert_eq!(expected, ron::ser::to_string_pretty(&value, pretty_config).unwrap());
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)/// // RON doesn't support borrowed deserialization of byte arrays
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)/// # }
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)/// ```
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)///
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)/// ## Alternative to [`BytesOrString`]
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)///
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)/// The [`Bytes`] can replace [`BytesOrString`].
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)/// [`Bytes`] is implemented for more types, which makes it better.
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)/// The serialization behavior of [`Bytes`] differs from [`BytesOrString`], therefore only `deserialize_as` should be used.
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)///
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)/// ```rust
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)/// # use serde::Deserialize;
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, Bytes};
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)/// #
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)/// #[serde_as]
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)/// #[derive(Deserialize, serde::Serialize)]
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)/// struct Test {
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)///     #[serde_as(deserialize_as = "Bytes")]
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)///     from_bytes: Vec<u8>,
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)///     #[serde_as(deserialize_as = "Bytes")]
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)///     from_str: Vec<u8>,
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)/// }
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)///
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)/// // Different serialized values ...
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)/// let j = json!({
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)///     "from_bytes": [70,111,111,45,66,97,114],
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)///     "from_str": "Foo-Bar",
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)/// });
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)///
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)/// // can be deserialized ...
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)/// let test = Test {
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)///     from_bytes: b"Foo-Bar".to_vec(),
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)///     from_str: b"Foo-Bar".to_vec(),
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)/// };
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)/// assert_eq!(test, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)///
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)/// // and serialization will always be a byte sequence
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)/// # assert_eq!(json!(
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)/// {
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)///     "from_bytes": [70,111,111,45,66,97,114],
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)///     "from_str": [70,111,111,45,66,97,114],
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)/// }
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)/// # ), serde_json::to_value(&test).unwrap());
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)/// # }
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)/// ```
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)pub struct [Bytes](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.Bytes.html);
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)/// Deserialize one or many elements
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)///
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)/// Sometimes it is desirable to have a shortcut in writing 1-element lists in a config file.
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)/// Usually, this is done by either writing a list or the list element itself.
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)/// This distinction is not semantically important on the Rust side, thus both forms should deserialize into the same `Vec`.
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)///
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)/// The `OneOrMany` adapter achieves exactly this use case.
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)/// The serialization behavior can be tweaked to either always serialize as a list using [`PreferMany`] or to serialize as the inner element if possible using [`PreferOne`].
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)/// By default, [`PreferOne`] is assumed, which can also be omitted like `OneOrMany<_>`.
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)///
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)/// [`PreferMany`]: crate::formats::PreferMany
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)/// [`PreferOne`]: crate::formats::PreferOne
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)///
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)/// # Examples
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)///
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)/// ```rust
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)/// # use serde::Deserialize;
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, OneOrMany};
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)/// # use serde_with::formats::{PreferOne, PreferMany};
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)/// #
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)/// #[serde_as]
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)/// #[derive(Deserialize, serde::Serialize)]
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)/// struct Data {
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)///     #[serde_as(as = "OneOrMany<_, PreferOne>")]
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)///     countries: Vec<String>,
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)///     #[serde_as(as = "OneOrMany<_, PreferMany>")]
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)///     cities: Vec<String>,
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)/// }
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)///
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)/// // The adapter allows deserializing a `Vec` from either
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)/// // a single element
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)/// let j = json!({
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)///     "countries": "Spain",
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)///     "cities": "Berlin",
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)/// });
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)/// assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Data>(j).is_ok());
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)///
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)/// // or from a list.
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)/// let j = json!({
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)///     "countries": ["Germany", "France"],
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)///     "cities": ["Amsterdam"],
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)/// });
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)/// assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Data>(j).is_ok());
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)///
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)/// // For serialization you can choose how a single element should be encoded.
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)/// // Either directly, with `PreferOne` (default), or as a list with `PreferMany`.
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)/// let data = Data {
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)///     countries: vec!["Spain".to_string()],
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)///     cities: vec!["Berlin".to_string()],
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)/// };
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)/// let j = json!({
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)///     "countries": "Spain",
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)///     "cities": ["Berlin"],
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)/// });
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)/// assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(data).unwrap(), j);
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)/// # }
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)/// ```
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)pub struct [OneOrMany](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.OneOrMany.html)<T: ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/trait.Sized.html), FORMAT: [formats::Format](https://docs.rs/formats.rs.html#11) = formats::[PreferOne](https://docs.rs/formats.rs.html#66-81)>(
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)    [PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<(FORMAT, T)>,
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768));
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)/// Try multiple deserialization options until one succeeds.
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)///
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)/// This adapter allows you to specify a list of deserialization options.
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)/// They are tried in order and the first one working is applied.
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)/// Serialization always picks the first option.
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)///
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)/// `PickFirst` has one type parameter which must be instantiated with a tuple of two, three, or four elements.
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)/// For example, `PickFirst<(_, DisplayFromStr)>` on a field of type `u32` allows deserializing from a number or from a string via the `FromStr` trait.
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)/// The value will be serialized as a number, since that is what the first type `_` indicates.
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)///
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)/// # Examples
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)///
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)/// Deserialize a number from either a number or a string.
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)///
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)/// ```rust
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, DisplayFromStr, PickFirst};
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)/// #
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)/// #[serde_as]
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)/// struct Data {
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)///     #[serde_as(as = "PickFirst<(_, DisplayFromStr)>")]
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)///     as_number: u32,
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)///     #[serde_as(as = "PickFirst<(DisplayFromStr, _)>")]
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)///     as_string: u32,
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)/// }
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)/// let data = Data {
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)///     as_number: 123,
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)///     as_string: 456
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)/// };
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)///
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)/// // Both fields can be deserialized from numbers:
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)/// let j = json!({
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)///     "as_number": 123,
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)///     "as_string": 456,
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)/// });
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)///
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)/// // or from a string:
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)/// let j = json!({
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)///     "as_number": "123",
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)///     "as_string": "456",
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)/// });
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)///
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)/// // For serialization the first type in the tuple determines the behavior.
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)/// // The `as_number` field will use the normal `Serialize` behavior and produce a number,
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)/// // while `as_string` used `Display` to produce a string.
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)/// let expected = json!({
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)///     "as_number": 123,
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)///     "as_string": "456",
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)/// });
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)/// assert_eq!(expected, serde_json::to_value(&data).unwrap());
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)/// # }
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)/// ```
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)pub struct [PickFirst](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.PickFirst.html)<T>([PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<T>);
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)/// Serialize value by converting to/from a proxy type with serde support.
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)///
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)/// This adapter serializes a type `O` by converting it into a second type `T` and serializing `T`.
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)/// Deserializing works analogue, by deserializing a `T` and then converting into `O`.
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)///
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)/// ```rust
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)/// # #[cfg(any())] {
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)/// struct S {
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)///     #[serde_as(as = "FromInto<T>")]
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)///     value: O,
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)/// }
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)/// # }
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)/// ```
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)///
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)/// For serialization `O` needs to be `O: Into<T> + Clone`.
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)/// For deserialization the opposite `T: Into<O>` is required.
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)/// The `Clone` bound is required since `serialize` operates on a reference but `Into` implementations on references are uncommon.
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)///
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)/// **Note**: [`TryFromInto`] is the more generalized version of this adapter which uses the [`TryInto`] trait instead.
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)///
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)/// # Example
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)///
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)/// ```rust
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)/// # use serde_json::json;
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, FromInto};
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)/// #
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)/// #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)/// struct Rgb {
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)///     red: u8,
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)///     green: u8,
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)///     blue: u8,
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)/// }
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)///
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)/// # /*
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)/// impl From<(u8, u8, u8)> for Rgb { ... }
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)/// impl From<Rgb> for (u8, u8, u8) { ... }
[1869](https://docs.rs#1869)/// # */
[1870](https://docs.rs#1870)/// #
[1871](https://docs.rs#1871)/// # impl From<(u8, u8, u8)> for Rgb {
[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)/// #     fn from(v: (u8, u8, u8)) -> Self {
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)/// #         Rgb {
[1874](https://docs.rs#1874)/// #             red: v.0,
[1875](https://docs.rs#1875)/// #             green: v.1,
[1876](https://docs.rs#1876)/// #             blue: v.2,
[1877](https://docs.rs#1877)/// #         }
[1878](https://docs.rs#1878)/// #     }
[1879](https://docs.rs#1879)/// # }
[1880](https://docs.rs#1880)/// #
[1881](https://docs.rs#1881)/// # impl From<Rgb> for (u8, u8, u8) {
[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)/// #     fn from(v: Rgb) -> Self {
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)/// #         (v.red, v.green, v.blue)
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)/// #     }
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)/// # }
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)///
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)/// #[serde_as]
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[1890](https://docs.rs#1890)/// struct Color {
[1891](https://docs.rs#1891)///     #[serde_as(as = "FromInto<(u8, u8, u8)>")]
[1892](https://docs.rs#1892)///     rgb: Rgb,
[1893](https://docs.rs#1893)/// }
[1894](https://docs.rs#1894)/// let color = Color {
[1895](https://docs.rs#1895)///     rgb: Rgb {
[1896](https://docs.rs#1896)///         red: 128,
[1897](https://docs.rs#1897)///         green: 64,
[1898](https://docs.rs#1898)///         blue: 32,
[1899](https://docs.rs#1899)///     },
[1900](https://docs.rs#1900)/// };
[1901](https://docs.rs#1901)///
[1902](https://docs.rs#1902)/// // Define our expected JSON form
[1903](https://docs.rs#1903)/// let j = json!({
[1904](https://docs.rs#1904)///     "rgb": [128, 64, 32],
[1905](https://docs.rs#1905)/// });
[1906](https://docs.rs#1906)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[1907](https://docs.rs#1907)/// assert_eq!(j, serde_json::to_value(&color).unwrap());
[1908](https://docs.rs#1908)/// assert_eq!(color, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[1909](https://docs.rs#1909)/// # }
[1910](https://docs.rs#1910)/// ```
[1911](https://docs.rs#1911)pub struct [FromInto](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.FromInto.html)<T>([PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<T>);

[1993](https://docs.rs#1993)
[1994](https://docs.rs#1994)/// Serialize value by converting to/from a proxy type with serde support.
[1995](https://docs.rs#1995)///
[1996](https://docs.rs#1996)/// This adapter serializes a type `O` by converting it into a second type `T` and serializing `T`.
[1997](https://docs.rs#1997)/// Deserializing works analogue, by deserializing a `T` and then converting into `O`.
[1998](https://docs.rs#1998)///
[1999](https://docs.rs#1999)/// ```rust
[2000](https://docs.rs#2000)/// # #[cfg(any())] {
[2001](https://docs.rs#2001)/// struct S {
[2002](https://docs.rs#2002)///     #[serde_as(as = "TryFromInto<T>")]
[2003](https://docs.rs#2003)///     value: O,
[2004](https://docs.rs#2004)/// }
[2005](https://docs.rs#2005)/// # }
[2006](https://docs.rs#2006)/// ```
[2007](https://docs.rs#2007)///
[2008](https://docs.rs#2008)/// For serialization `O` needs to be `O: TryInto<T> + Clone`.
[2009](https://docs.rs#2009)/// For deserialization the opposite `T: TryInto<O>` is required.
[2010](https://docs.rs#2010)/// The `Clone` bound is required since `serialize` operates on a reference but `TryInto` implementations on references are uncommon.
[2011](https://docs.rs#2011)/// In both cases the `TryInto::Error` type must implement [`Display`](std::fmt::Display).
[2012](https://docs.rs#2012)///
[2013](https://docs.rs#2013)/// **Note**: [`FromInto`] is the more specialized version of this adapter which uses the infallible [`Into`] trait instead.
[2014](https://docs.rs#2014)/// [`TryFromInto`] is strictly more general and can also be used where [`FromInto`] is applicable.
[2015](https://docs.rs#2015)/// The example shows a use case, when only the deserialization behavior is fallible, but not serializing.
[2016](https://docs.rs#2016)///
[2017](https://docs.rs#2017)/// # Example
[2018](https://docs.rs#2018)///
[2019](https://docs.rs#2019)/// ```rust

[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)/// Serialize a reference value by converting to/from a proxy type with serde support.
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)///
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)/// This adapter serializes a type `O` by converting it into a second type `T` and serializing `T`.
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)/// Deserializing works analogue, by deserializing a `T` and then converting into `O`.
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)///
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)/// ```rust
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)/// # #[cfg(any())] {
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)/// struct S {
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)///     #[serde_as(as = "TryFromIntoRef<T>")]
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)///     value: O,
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)/// }
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)/// # }
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)/// ```
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)///
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)/// For serialization `O` needs to be `for<'a> &'a O: TryInto<T>`.
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)/// For deserialization the opposite `T: TryInto<O>` is required.
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)/// In both cases the `TryInto::Error` type must implement [`Display`](std::fmt::Display).
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)///
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)/// **Note**: [`FromIntoRef`] is the more specialized version of this adapter which uses the infallible [`Into`] trait instead.
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)/// [`TryFromIntoRef`] is strictly more general and can also be used where [`FromIntoRef`] is applicable.
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)/// The example shows a use case, when only the deserialization behavior is fallible, but not serializing.
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)///
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)/// # Example
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)///
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)/// ```rust
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)/// # use serde_json::json;
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, TryFromIntoRef};
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)/// #
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)/// enum Boollike {
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)///     True,
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)///     False,
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)/// }
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)///
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)/// # /*
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)/// impl<'a> From<&'a Boollike> for u8 { ... }
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)/// # */
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)/// #
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)/// impl TryFrom<u8> for Boollike {
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)///     type Error = String;
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)///     fn try_from(v: u8) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)///         match v {
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)///             0 => Ok(Boollike::False),
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)///             1 => Ok(Boollike::True),
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)///             _ => Err(format!("Boolikes can only be constructed from 0 or 1 but found {}", v))
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)///         }
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)///     }
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)/// }
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)/// #
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)/// # impl<'a> From<&'a Boollike> for u8 {
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)/// #     fn from(v: &'a Boollike) -> Self {
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)/// #        match v {
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)/// #            Boollike::True => 1,
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)/// #            Boollike::False => 0,
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)/// #        }
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)/// #     }
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)/// # }
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)///
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)/// #[serde_as]
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)/// struct Data {
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)///     #[serde_as(as = "TryFromIntoRef<u8>")]
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)///     b: Boollike,
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)/// }
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)/// let data = Data {
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)///     b: Boollike::True,
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)/// };
[2153](https://docs.rs#2153)///
[2154](https://docs.rs#2154)/// // Define our expected JSON form
[2155](https://docs.rs#2155)/// let j = json!({
[2156](https://docs.rs#2156)///     "b": 1,
[2157](https://docs.rs#2157)/// });
[2158](https://docs.rs#2158)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[2159](https://docs.rs#2159)/// assert_eq!(j, serde_json::to_value(&data).unwrap());
[2160](https://docs.rs#2160)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[2161](https://docs.rs#2161)///
[2162](https://docs.rs#2162)/// // Numbers besides 0 or 1 should be an error
[2163](https://docs.rs#2163)/// let j = json!({
[2164](https://docs.rs#2164)///     "b": 2,
[2165](https://docs.rs#2165)/// });
[2166](https://docs.rs#2166)/// assert_eq!("Boolikes can only be constructed from 0 or 1 but found 2", serde_json::from_value::<Data>(j).unwrap_err().to_string());
[2167](https://docs.rs#2167)/// # }
[2168](https://docs.rs#2168)/// ```
[2169](https://docs.rs#2169)pub struct [TryFromIntoRef](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.TryFromIntoRef.html)<T>([PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<T>);

[2171](https://docs.rs#2171)/// Borrow `Cow` data during deserialization when possible.
[2172](https://docs.rs#2172)///
[2173](https://docs.rs#2173)/// The types `Cow<'a, [u8]>`, `Cow<'a, [u8; N]>`, and `Cow<'a, str>` can borrow from the input data during deserialization.
[2174](https://docs.rs#2174)/// serde supports this, by annotating the fields with `#[serde(borrow)]`. but does not support borrowing on nested types.
[2175](https://docs.rs#2175)/// This gap is filled by this `BorrowCow` adapter.
[2176](https://docs.rs#2176)///
[2177](https://docs.rs#2177)/// Using this adapter with `Cow<'a, [u8]>`/`Cow<'a, [u8; N]>` will serialize the value as a sequence of `u8` values.
[2178](https://docs.rs#2178)/// This *might* not allow to borrow the data during deserialization.
[2179](https://docs.rs#2179)/// For a different format, which is also more efficient, use the [`Bytes`] adapter, which is also implemented for `Cow`.
[2180](https://docs.rs#2180)///
[2181](https://docs.rs#2181)/// When combined with the [`serde_as`] attribute, the `#[serde(borrow)]` annotation will be added automatically.
[2182](https://docs.rs#2182)/// If the annotation is wrong or too broad, for example because of multiple lifetime parameters, a manual annotation is required.
[2183](https://docs.rs#2183)///
[2184](https://docs.rs#2184)/// # Examples
[2185](https://docs.rs#2185)///
[2186](https://docs.rs#2186)/// ```rust
[2187](https://docs.rs#2187)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2188](https://docs.rs#2188)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2189](https://docs.rs#2189)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, BorrowCow};
[2190](https://docs.rs#2190)/// # use std::borrow::Cow;
[2191](https://docs.rs#2191)/// #
[2192](https://docs.rs#2192)/// #[serde_as]
[2193](https://docs.rs#2193)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)/// struct Data<'a, 'b, 'c> {
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)///     #[serde_as(as = "BorrowCow")]
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)///     str: Cow<'a, str>,
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)///     #[serde_as(as = "BorrowCow")]
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)///     slice: Cow<'b, [u8]>,
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)///
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)///     #[serde_as(as = "Option<[BorrowCow; 1]>")]
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)///     nested: Option<[Cow<'c, str>; 1]>,
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)/// }
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)/// let data = Data {
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)///     str: "foobar".into(),
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)///     slice: b"foobar"[..].into(),
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)///     nested: Some(["HelloWorld".into()]),
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)/// };
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)///
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)/// // Define our expected JSON form
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)/// let j = r#"{
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)///   "str": "foobar",
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)///   "slice": [
[2214](https://docs.rs#2214)///     102,
[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)///     111,
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)///     111,
[2217](https://docs.rs#2217)///     98,
[2218](https://docs.rs#2218)///     97,
[2219](https://docs.rs#2219)///     114
[2220](https://docs.rs#2220)///   ],
[2221](https://docs.rs#2221)///   "nested": [
[2222](https://docs.rs#2222)///     "HelloWorld"
[2223](https://docs.rs#2223)///   ]
[2224](https://docs.rs#2224)/// }"#;
[2225](https://docs.rs#2225)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[2226](https://docs.rs#2226)/// assert_eq!(j, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&data).unwrap());
[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_str(j).unwrap());
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)///
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)/// // Cow borrows from the input data
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)/// let deserialized: Data<'_, '_, '_> = serde_json::from_str(j).unwrap();
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)/// assert!(matches!(deserialized.str, Cow::Borrowed(_)));
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)/// assert!(matches!(deserialized.nested, Some([Cow::Borrowed(_)])));
[2233](https://docs.rs#2233)/// // JSON does not allow borrowing bytes, so `slice` does not borrow
[2234](https://docs.rs#2234)/// assert!(matches!(deserialized.slice, Cow::Owned(_)));
[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)/// # }
[2236](https://docs.rs#2236)/// ```
[2237](https://docs.rs#2237)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[2238](https://docs.rs#2238)pub struct [BorrowCow](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.BorrowCow.html);

[2240](https://docs.rs#2240)/// A trait to inspect skipped deserialization errors
[2241](https://docs.rs#2241)///
[2242](https://docs.rs#2242)/// The [`VecSkipError`] and [`MapSkipError`] adapters allow to skip values which fail to deserialize.
[2243](https://docs.rs#2243)/// This trait allows inspecting these errors, for example for logging purposes.
[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)///
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)/// The trait has a single method [`inspect_error`][InspectError::inspect_error], which will be called for each deserialization error.
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)/// The default implementation for `()` does nothing.
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)///
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)/// See the documentation of [`VecSkipError`] and [`MapSkipError`] for usage examples.
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]

[2251](https://docs.rs#2251)    /// Inspect a deserialization error which was skipped.
[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)    fn inspect_error(error: impl [serde_core::de::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Error.html));
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)}
[2254](https://docs.rs#2254)
[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)impl [InspectError](https://docs.rs#2250-2253) for () {
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)    fn inspect_error(_error: impl [serde_core::de::Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Error.html)) {}
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)}

[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)/// Deserialize a sequence into `Vec<T>`, skipping elements which fail to deserialize.
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)///
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)/// The serialization behavior is identical to `Vec<T>`. This is an alternative to `Vec<T>`
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)/// which is resilient against unexpected data.
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)///
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)/// You can be notified of skipped elements by providing a type that implements the [`InspectError`] trait.
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)/// The second generic argument `I` defaults to `()`, which does nothing.
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)///
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)/// # Examples
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)///
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)/// ## Basic Usage
[2271](https://docs.rs#2271)///
[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)/// ```rust
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, VecSkipError};
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)/// #
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)/// # #[non_exhaustive]
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)/// enum Color {
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)///     Red,
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)///     Green,
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)///     Blue,
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)/// }
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)/// # use Color::*;
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)/// #[serde_as]
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)/// struct Palette(#[serde_as(as = "VecSkipError<_>")] Vec<Color>);
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)///
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)/// let data = Palette(vec![Blue, Green,]);
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)/// let source_json = r#"["Blue", "Yellow", "Green"]"#;
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)/// let data_json = r#"["Blue","Green"]"#;
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)/// assert_eq!(data_json, serde_json::to_string(&data).unwrap());
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_str(source_json).unwrap());
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)/// # }
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)/// ```
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)///
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)/// ## Using [`InspectError`](`crate::InspectError`) to log skipped elements
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)///
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)/// ```rust
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)/// # #[cfg(all(feature = "macros", feature = "alloc"))] {
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)/// # use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, InspectError, VecSkipError};
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)/// # use std::cell::RefCell;
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)///
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)/// struct ErrorInspector;
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)///
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)/// thread_local! {
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)///     static ERRORS: RefCell<Vec<String>> = RefCell::new(Vec::new());
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)/// }
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)///
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)/// impl InspectError for ErrorInspector {
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)///     fn inspect_error(error: impl serde::de::Error) {
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)///         ERRORS.with(|errors| errors.borrow_mut().push(error.to_string()));
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)///     }
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)/// }
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)///
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)/// #[serde_as]
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)/// struct S {
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)///     tag: String,
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)///     #[serde_as(as = "VecSkipError<_, ErrorInspector>")]
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)///     values: Vec<u8>,
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)/// }
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)///
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)/// let json = r#"{"tag":"type","values":[0, "str", 1, [10, 11], -2, {}, 300]}"#;
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)/// let s: S = serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap();
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)/// assert_eq!(s.values, vec![0, 1]);
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)///
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)/// let errors = ERRORS.with(|errors| errors.borrow().clone());
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)/// eprintln!("Errors: {errors:#?}");
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)/// assert_eq!(errors.len(), 5);
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)/// assert!(errors[0].contains("invalid type: string \"str\", expected u8"));
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)/// assert!(errors[1].contains("invalid type: sequence, expected u8"));
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)/// assert!(errors[2].contains("invalid value: integer `-2`, expected u8"));
[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)/// assert!(errors[3].contains("invalid type: map, expected u8"));
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)/// assert!(errors[4].contains("invalid value: integer `300`, expected u8"));
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)/// # }
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)/// ```
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)pub struct [VecSkipError](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.VecSkipError.html)<T, I = ()>([PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<(T, I)>);
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)/// Deserialize a map, skipping keys and values which fail to deserialize.
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)///
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)/// By default serde terminates if it fails to deserialize a key or a value when deserializing
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)/// a map. Sometimes a map has heterogeneous keys or values but we only care about some specific
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)/// types, and it is desirable to skip entries on errors.
[2350](https://docs.rs#2350)///
[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)/// You can be notified of skipped elements by providing a type that implements the [`InspectError`] trait.
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)/// The third generic argument `I` defaults to `()`, which does nothing.
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)///
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)/// It is especially useful in conjunction to `#[serde(flatten)]` to capture a map mixed in with
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)/// other entries which we don't want to exhaust in the type definition.
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)///
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)/// The serialization behavior is identical to the underlying map.
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)///
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)/// The implementation supports both the [`HashMap`] and the [`BTreeMap`] from the standard library.
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)///
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)/// [`BTreeMap`]: std::collections::BTreeMap
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)/// [`HashMap`]: std::collections::HashMap
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)///
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)/// # Examples
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)///
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)/// ## Basic Usage
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)///
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)/// ```rust
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)/// # use std::collections::BTreeMap;
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, DisplayFromStr, MapSkipError};
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)/// #
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)/// #[serde_as]
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)/// struct VersionNames {
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)///     yanked: Vec<u16>,
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)///     #[serde_as(as = "MapSkipError<DisplayFromStr, _>")]
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)///     #[serde(flatten)]
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)///     names: BTreeMap<u16, String>,
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)/// }
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)///
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)/// let data = VersionNames {
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)///     yanked: vec![2, 5],
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)///     names: BTreeMap::from_iter([
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)///         (0u16, "v0".to_string()),
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)///         (1, "v1".to_string()),
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)///         (4, "v4".to_string())
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)///     ]),
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)/// };
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)/// let source_json = r#"{
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)///   "0": "v0",
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)///   "1": "v1",
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)///   "4": "v4",
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)///   "yanked": [2, 5],
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)///   "last_updated": 1704085200
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)/// }"#;
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)/// let data_json = r#"{"yanked":[2,5],"0":"v0","1":"v1","4":"v4"}"#;
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)/// assert_eq!(data_json, serde_json::to_string(&data).unwrap());
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_str(source_json).unwrap());
[2403](https://docs.rs#2403)/// # }
[2404](https://docs.rs#2404)/// ```
[2405](https://docs.rs#2405)///
[2406](https://docs.rs#2406)/// ## Using [`InspectError`](`crate::InspectError`) to log skipped elements
[2407](https://docs.rs#2407)///
[2408](https://docs.rs#2408)/// ```rust
[2409](https://docs.rs#2409)/// # #[cfg(all(feature = "macros", feature = "alloc"))] {
[2410](https://docs.rs#2410)/// # use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize};
[2411](https://docs.rs#2411)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, InspectError, MapSkipError};
[2412](https://docs.rs#2412)/// # use std::collections::BTreeMap;
[2413](https://docs.rs#2413)/// # use std::cell::RefCell;
[2414](https://docs.rs#2414)///
[2415](https://docs.rs#2415)/// struct ErrorInspector;
[2416](https://docs.rs#2416)///
[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)/// thread_local! {
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)///     static ERRORS: RefCell<Vec<String>> = RefCell::new(Vec::new());
[2419](https://docs.rs#2419)/// }
[2420](https://docs.rs#2420)///
[2421](https://docs.rs#2421)/// impl InspectError for ErrorInspector {
[2422](https://docs.rs#2422)///     fn inspect_error(error: impl serde::de::Error) {
[2423](https://docs.rs#2423)///         ERRORS.with(|errors| errors.borrow_mut().push(error.to_string()));
[2424](https://docs.rs#2424)///     }
[2425](https://docs.rs#2425)/// }
[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)///
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)/// #[serde_as]
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)/// struct S {
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)///     tag: String,
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)///     #[serde_as(as = "MapSkipError<_, _, ErrorInspector>")]
[2432](https://docs.rs#2432)///     values: BTreeMap<String, u8>,
[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)/// }
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)///
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)/// let json = r#"{"tag":"type","values":{"valid":42,"invalid": null,"another":"str","nested":[1,2,3]}}"#;
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)/// let s: S = serde_json::from_str(json).unwrap();
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)/// assert_eq!(s.values.len(), 1);
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)/// assert_eq!(s.values.get("valid"), Some(&42));
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)///
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)/// let errors = ERRORS.with(|errors| errors.borrow().clone());
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)/// assert_eq!(errors.len(), 3);
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)/// eprintln!("Errors: {errors:#?}");
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)/// assert!(errors[0].contains("invalid type: null, expected u8"));
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)/// assert!(errors[1].contains("invalid type: string \"str\", expected u8"));
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)/// assert!(errors[2].contains("invalid type: sequence, expected u8"));
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)/// # }
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)/// ```
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)#[cfg(feature = "alloc")]

[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)/// Deserialize a boolean from a number
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)///
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)/// Deserialize a number (of `u8`) and turn it into a boolean.
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)/// The adapter supports a [`Strict`](crate::formats::Strict) and [`Flexible`](crate::formats::Flexible) format.
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)/// In `Strict` mode, the number must be `0` or `1`.
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)/// All other values produce an error.
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)/// In `Flexible` mode, the number any non-zero value is converted to `true`.
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)///
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)/// During serialization only `0` or `1` are ever emitted.
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)///
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)/// # Examples
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)///
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)/// ```rust
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)/// # use serde_json::json;
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, BoolFromInt};
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)/// #
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)/// #[serde_as]
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)/// struct Data(#[serde_as(as = "BoolFromInt")] bool);
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)///
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)/// let data = Data(true);
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)/// let j = json!(1);
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)/// // Ensure serialization and deserialization produce the expected results
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)/// assert_eq!(j, serde_json::to_value(&data).unwrap());
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)///
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)/// // false maps to 0
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)/// let data = Data(false);
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)/// let j = json!(0);
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)/// assert_eq!(j, serde_json::to_value(&data).unwrap());
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)//
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)/// #[serde_as]
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)/// struct Flexible(#[serde_as(as = "BoolFromInt<serde_with::formats::Flexible>")] bool);
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)///
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)/// // Flexible turns any non-zero number into true
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)/// let data = Flexible(true);
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)/// let j = json!(100);
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(j).unwrap());
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)/// # }
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)/// ```
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)pub struct [BoolFromInt](https://docs.rs/serde_with/struct.BoolFromInt.html)<S: [formats::Strictness](https://docs.rs/formats.rs.html#86) = formats::[Strict](https://docs.rs/formats.rs.html#89)>([PhantomData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/struct.PhantomData.html)<S>);

[2603](https://docs.rs#2603)/// De/Serialize a Map into a list of tuples
[2604](https://docs.rs#2604)///
[2605](https://docs.rs#2605)/// Some formats, like JSON, have limitations on the types of keys for maps.
[2606](https://docs.rs#2606)/// In case of JSON, keys are restricted to strings.
[2607](https://docs.rs#2607)/// Rust features more powerful keys, for example tuples, which can not be serialized to JSON.
[2608](https://docs.rs#2608)///
[2609](https://docs.rs#2609)/// This helper serializes the Map into a list of tuples, which do not have the same type restrictions.
[2610](https://docs.rs#2610)///
[2611](https://docs.rs#2611)/// # Examples
[2612](https://docs.rs#2612)///
[2613](https://docs.rs#2613)/// ```rust
[2614](https://docs.rs#2614)/// # #[cfg(feature = "macros")] {
[2615](https://docs.rs#2615)/// # use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
[2616](https://docs.rs#2616)/// # use serde_json::json;
[2617](https://docs.rs#2617)/// # use serde_with::{serde_as, Seq};
[2618](https://docs.rs#2618)/// # use std::collections::BTreeMap;
[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)/// #
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)/// #[serde_as]
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)/// # #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
[2622](https://docs.rs#2622)/// #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)/// struct A {
[2624](https://docs.rs#2624)///     #[serde_as(as = "Seq<(_, _)>")]
[2625](https://docs.rs#2625)///     s: BTreeMap<(String, u32), u32>,
[2626](https://docs.rs#2626)/// }
[2627](https://docs.rs#2627)///
[2628](https://docs.rs#2628)/// // This converts the Rust type
[2629](https://docs.rs#2629)/// let data = A {
[2630](https://docs.rs#2630)///     s: BTreeMap::from([
[2631](https://docs.rs#2631)///         (("Hello".to_string(), 123), 0),
[2632](https://docs.rs#2632)///         (("World".to_string(), 456), 1),
[2633](https://docs.rs#2633)///     ]),
[2634](https://docs.rs#2634)/// };
[2635](https://docs.rs#2635)///
[2636](https://docs.rs#2636)/// // into this JSON
[2637](https://docs.rs#2637)/// let value = json!({
[2638](https://docs.rs#2638)///     "s": [
[2639](https://docs.rs#2639)///         [["Hello", 123], 0],
[2640](https://docs.rs#2640)///         [["World", 456], 1]
[2641](https://docs.rs#2641)///     ]
[2642](https://docs.rs#2642)/// });
[2643](https://docs.rs#2643)///
[2644](https://docs.rs#2644)/// assert_eq!(value, serde_json::to_value(&data).unwrap());
[2645](https://docs.rs#2645)/// assert_eq!(data, serde_json::from_value(value).unwrap());
[2646](https://docs.rs#2646)/// # }

# DeserializeAs in serde_with - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_with/3.21.0/serde_with/trait.DeserializeAs.html

`pub trait DeserializeAs<'de, T>: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [deserialize_as](https://docs.rs#tymethod.deserialize_as)<D>(deserializer: D) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<T, D::[Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserializer.html#associatedtype.Error)>
       where D: [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserializer.html)<'de>;
}## Expand description

A **data structure** that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde, analogue to [ Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html).

The trait is analogue to the [ serde::Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html) trait, with the same meaning of input and output arguments.
It can and should be implemented using the same code structure as the

[trait. As such, the same advice for](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html)

`Deserialize`[implementing](https://serde.rs/impl-deserialize.html)applies here.

`Deserialize`[§](https://docs.rs#differences-to-deserialize)Differences to `Deserialize`

`Deserialize`The trait is only required for container-like types or types implementing specific conversion functions.
Container-like types are [ Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html),

[, but also](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)

`BTreeMap`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html)

`Option`[. Conversion types deserialize into a different Rust type. For example,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box`[uses the](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayFromStr.html)

`DisplayFromStr`[trait after deserializing a string and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/str/traits/trait.FromStr.html)

`FromStr`[creates a](https://docs.rs/struct.DurationSeconds.html)

`DurationSeconds`[from either String or integer values.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/time/struct.Duration.html)

`Duration`This code shows how to implement [ Deserialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.226/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html) for

[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box`[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
impl<'de, T: Deserialize<'de>> Deserialize<'de> for Box<T> {
    fn deserialize<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error>
    where
        D: Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        Ok(Box::new(Deserialize::deserialize(deserializer)?))
    }
}
```
and this code shows how to do the same using [ DeserializeAs](https://docs.rs/trait.DeserializeAs.html):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
impl<'de, T, U> DeserializeAs<'de, Box<T>> for Box<U>
where
    U: DeserializeAs<'de, T>,
{
    fn deserialize_as<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Box<T>, D::Error>
    where
        D: Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        Ok(Box::new(
            DeserializeAsWrap::<T, U>::deserialize(deserializer)?.into_inner(),
        ))
    }
}
```
It uses two type parameters, `T` and `U` instead of only one and performs the deserialization step using the `DeserializeAsWrap` type.
The `T` type is the type on the Rust side after deserialization, whereas the `U` type determines how the value will be deserialized.
These two changes are usually enough to make a container type implement [ DeserializeAs](https://docs.rs/trait.DeserializeAs.html).

[ DeserializeAsWrap](https://docs.rs/de/struct.DeserializeAsWrap.html) is a piece of glue code which turns

[into a serde compatible datatype, by converting all calls to](https://docs.rs/trait.DeserializeAs.html)

`DeserializeAs``deserialize` into `deserialize_as`.
This allows us to implement [such that it can be applied recursively throughout the whole data structure. This is mostly important for container types, such as](https://docs.rs/trait.DeserializeAs.html)

`DeserializeAs``Vec` or `BTreeMap`.
In a `BTreeMap` this allows us to specify two different serialization behaviors, one for key and one for value, using the [trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.DeserializeAs.html)

`DeserializeAs`[§](https://docs.rs#implementing-a-converter-type)Implementing a converter Type

This shows a simplified implementation for [ DisplayFromStr](https://docs.rs/struct.DisplayFromStr.html).

```
struct DisplayFromStr;
impl<'de, T> DeserializeAs<'de, T> for DisplayFromStr
where
    T: FromStr,
    T::Err: Display,
{
    fn deserialize_as<D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<T, D::Error>
    where
        D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
    {
        let s = String::deserialize(deserializer).map_err(Error::custom)?;
        s.parse().map_err(Error::custom)
    }
}
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*
